title: Standard Keycloak login issues a session and GET /api/client/users/me resolves permissions without error
preconditions: A seeded test user with a real role exists in the target environment
steps: Log in through the standard Keycloak OAuth flow
expectedResult: 200 OK with a well-formed user object including a permissions array (possibly empty for NORMAL_USER) and roleIds populated — no 401/500.

title: Org Admin (SUPERADMIN) can open every top-level module without a 403
preconditions: Logged in as an org's SUPERADMIN (Org Admin)
steps: Visit each top-level nav module in turn: Evidence, Policy, Audit, Risk, Vendors, Trust Vault, GRC Framework, Organization, Billing
expectedResult: Every page renders its normal content with no Access Denied page and no 403 API responses in the network tab.

title: A user with zero permissions gets 403, never 500, on a permission-gated route
description: loadPermissions.js's catch block (line 306-314) degrades to an empty permission Set on any resolution error rather than crashing the request; requirePermission then produces a clean 403.
preconditions: User with NORMAL_USER role and no project memberships
expectedResult: 403 Forbidden with the standard {success:false, message:'Missing permission: evidence.read'} shape — never a 500 or an unhandled exception.

title: JWKS endpoint is reachable and getJwksClient() initializes without throwing in the target environment
description: authenticate.js:12-22. If KEYCLOAK_ISSUER is misconfigured or unreachable, every real (non-bypass) authenticated request fails with 401 'Authentication service unavailable' — a fast, environment-level sanity check before running any deeper RBAC suite.
steps: Send one authenticated request with a real Bearer token through vibrantix-backend
expectedResult: The JWKS endpoint returns a valid key set (200, JSON with 'keys' array). The authenticated request succeeds without an 'auth.jwks.unavailable' or 'auth.jwks.error' log entry.

title: An expired JWT returns a clean 401, not a crash or silent pass-through
description: authenticate.js:252-262 explicitly catches jwt TokenExpiredError and returns 401 'Token expired'.
steps: Send a request with a Bearer token whose exp claim is in the past
expectedResult: 401 {success:false, message:'Token expired'} — request never reaches loadPermissions or any controller.
